rows: A barely visible crack down the centre of the ancient edifice spits out dust. The monolith shakes, and two vast doors swing open. The interior of the ancient structure is hollow, and has been used as a burial chamber.
A beak emerges from the ancient stone. It's shouting, but can't be heard. In the stone above someone, long ago, has scrawled advice for those who would approach it.
Feed beak common catalyst or Feed beak uncommon catalyst
A biological probe antenna launches from the terminal and fuses with my exosuit. I can't move.
A faint chill can be felt while the security alert sounds. Coolant pipes are flushed, and an automated report appears on-screen.
A mass-mailed off-world message shows damaged electronic lifeforms. Arms are ripped off, masks chewed and facial lights dimmed.
Reply with units or Reply with outrage
A screen detailing production conditions is open.
A small winged creature lands on the very top of the monolith. Suddenly, its eyes glow red and its head revolves in a full circle. It screams for mercy in an ancient voice that wants itself dead.
A strange test is visible on the terminal. A resident Trader has left a note for a colleague.
Help creature, then sell it water
A trade vault shakes, and closer inspection reveals that it's full of writhing molluscs. They are pink and slug-like, with sharp bloodied teeth.
A warrior has booby-trapped the terminal. The security alert has triggered the timer on an explosive charge. There are two wires exposed.
Alarms blare, sounding out against my intrusion. The facility is remotely operated, and no-one responds to the klaxon's call.

Alarms echo across the facility, a warning against my intrusion. Such an alert does not appear to slow down the commercial needs of the Gek, however. A nearby trade-ship is hailing the facility, looking for goods.
An ancient warrior's feet and legs slowly emerge from the bottom of the monolith. The rest of their torso then follows, unceremoniously pushed out onto the bare rock. They have been decapitated.
An animated gilled blob is on-screen waving a gun. It talks in the language of the warriors, but brightly and happily.
An automated report finished just before my incursion. As it did so, laser beams in resource vaults dimmed.
An automatic process has scrambled the output of the terminal. I can make out a few words, but the rest is lost in static.
An empty shell of an electronic lifeform emerges from the monolith. It is ancient and weather-beaten. The light in its mask has been extinguished for many centuries.
An off-world command priority has stalled all processes within this installation. The terminal blinks angrily with a demand for urgent action on an unpaid debt.
An unknown fault has forced the whole system offline. There is a strange chill in the air, a sharp clarity to the atmosphere.
As I study the ancient runes, they begin to glow with an ethereal light. I can see wisps of a strange blue energy being pulled from the obelisk and swirling around my Multi-Tool.
As my feet approach the Monolith, I hear a low rumble, which gradually builds into an ancient scream. It's like no other noise I've ever experienced.
As the floods through the monolith, images flood into my head, seizing my mind as their own.
Destroy the vandal or Scream for aid
As the resonates within the monolith, words written in my own language glow faintly on its surface. I reach out to touch the runes...
Strain against it or Embrace decay
Bathe in our waters. Feel Korvax Echoes calm. Bathe in our waters. Feel Korvax Echoes calm.
Beware! Murderous abomination! Do not awake! Terror! Despair! Do not awake!
Calm, child. Calm. We are with you.
Despite the security alert machines are operational. My scanner flashes briefly with the element varieties used to fuel them.
Emergency measures have been initialised. The timestamp on the terminal's error reporting display shows that the incident occured long before my intrusion.
First Spawn demand tax. Pay units immediately.

For many ages it appears that pilgrims have carved numerical figures between the glowing glyphs of the monolith. Looking down, I notice an ancient coin. I scrape the ground with my boot, and unearth several more.
Fuel given. Ice thaws. Vy'keen rise. Fuel given. Ice thaws. Vy'keen rise.
Grah! Gek war preparation disrupted! Ammunition production stalled! Metal required!
Grah! Initiate sentinel blood processing! Vaults full! Grah! Glass and blood! Glass and blood!
High Command demand explanation! Scare element required! Demand chromatic metal! Restore contributions!
Issue counter-order or Insert Chromatic Metal
Hirk took the treasure of Nal after battle. Treasure now hides in the city of Hirk.

I am an observer. I witness beaked traders dressed in modern Exosuits leaving an object at the base of a Monolith. It is a small mesh of wires and canisters. They charge it with a strange metal, then quickly depart.
I am not alone. Tiny beaked creatures gambol around my feet. To them I am a giant, and they recoil in terror when they see me towering above them.
I approach the terminal and search for a way to override the alarm. I find a likely looking button and press it, causing the terminal to respond.
I approach the terminal, but something deep within the complex is malfunctioning. Surfaces feel hot to the touch, hidden machinery clanks and whirrs. An alert sounds:
I approach the terminal, but the readout is confusing, garbled...
Shut down production or Report to Gek authorities
I approach the terminal. A message blinks, ready to send.
Send stock list or Uncheck one item and send

I begin to feel dizzy. A strange lethargy comes over me, and I feel compelled to lie down in front of the ancient relic. This place feels calming. It feels like home, wherever that might have once been.
I discover an excited message from off-world. It seems to be discussing a report with... an image of me at its centre!

I feel I am being watched. I turn, but can't see the potential assailant. But I know, with burning certainty, that they are there. Somewhere out there on the alien landscape, someone is about to launch an attack.
I feel an intense heat burning within the rock. Suddenly, as if attracted to my suit, a liquid metal starts to seep from a hole that's been broken into the rock. A voice screams out.
I feel faint. Ill, even. Looking around, the vegetation that surrounds this ancient structure looks withered and sickly. The creatures of the planet, meanwhile, appear to keep their distance.
I find a report filled with images of Sentinels, but its upload seems to have stalled.
I hear the distant voices of the Korvax entities who once worshipped here. And yet, there are other voices - discordant, unmistakeable, growing ever louder. I close my eyes, and listen.
I open a list of military achievements that's waiting for upload. There are images of distant battles, bloodied robots and vast explosions.
I open the terminal, looking for a way to shut off the alarm. Primary access appears to be via some sort of hand scanner.
I place my hands upon this relic, and I feel the power of this ancient site pulse through my veins. Words begin to take shape in my mind...
Close my mind or Open my mind
I place my palm on the monolith, then stand back when it melts in response to my touch. Molten rock drips down the stone, exposing a hollow interior.
I rapidly flick through alien warnings to discover what's brought the facility offline.
I run my hands across the monolith's surface, my fingers reading its ancient runes. Suddenly, I am seized by some ancient power, its otherworldly vision replacing my own.
I see a ragged claw grab at me. Despite being broken and fragmented, it holds me tight while a metallic beak emerges from the living rock.
Interference from the security alert has turned the screen to static. I can hardly make out anything beyond a few words.
Interloper detection! Heat detection systems confirm report! High temperature intruder!
Intruder alert! Commence detonation sequence! Organic fuel flow initiated!
Block fuel lines or Shutdown catalyst pipes
Intruder detected! Respiration gas concentration high! Enemy respiration!!
Hold breath or Deploy Vy'keen Dagger
Korvax Echoes will advance the Traveller. Korvax Echoes will advance Traveller's technology.
Machinery here is mining a captured asteroid for oxides. The process has stalled. The facility reeks of burnt metal, and the floor is hot to touch. I search the terminal for clues.
Machinery is still active. A timer ticks slowly down to the facility's next roll-out of products.
Major security alert! Interloper detected! Minor alert: war factory entrance door destroyed.
Military insignia and images of recently destroyed Sentinels fill the screen. Alien propaganda imagery takes glory in the destruction.
Input a huge number or Input a small number
My entry has caused the facility to go into immediate lockdown, interrupting its operation. Readouts on the terminal indicate some sort of deep-level exploratory or drilling operation.
Recall probe or Restart probe, then Recall probe

My entry has caused the facility to go into immediate lockdown, interrupting its operation. Visual readouts on the terminal indicate that this is a deep-level mining facility. Its resource vaults are emptying rapidly.
My hand rests upon the cool stone of the monolith. A voice, piercing, cries out in response to my touch.
Give in or Wait or Resist
My hands are drawn irresistibly towards the monolith, its ancient surface alive with the power of .
Build a head from Sentinel parts or Build legs from starship parts or Build arms from Multi-Tool parts
My intrusion has led to the work underway on the primary terminal being scrambled. It's a jumble of words.
My intrusion has triggered some sort of scrambled shutdown. Even over the sound of the alarm, I can hear the rumble of elements cascading away through the pipes. The terminal blinks a warning:
Override security alert or Inject coolant
My unauthorised intrusion has activated an alert on the control terminal. Its lights flash an angry, hostile red.
Operations are offline. A recent research scan has been corrupted, likely by my unexpected interruption. It is crashing every system in the outpost.
Past is dead. Youth is over. Only the traveller journey remains.
Pathetic warrior learn Vy'keen language! Pass test or encounter fighting pits! ERROR ERROR INSERT CATALYST ERROR ERROR MALFUNCTION

Reams of data are flowing into this terminal from research outposts all over the planet. As well as a storage depot for the planetary products locked away in the vaults beneath my feet, this is a point of transmission.
Rebuild the ancient warrior body. Restore monolith power. Make body whole again.
Respect the Vy'keen Ancients sacrifice. The beast has holy sight. Respect holy sacrifice.
Respect the Warrior! Respect their weapon!
Retain foul First Spawn stench! Remove sweet eggs from the spawning syrup!
Security breach! Military action unstoppable! Vy'keen High Command vessel coordinate upload imminent!
Broadcast safety code or Hack in safety code
Security systems have reacted to my unauthorised entry. The terminal barks a series of warnings.
Submit cancellation request or Activate fire extinguishers
Strange symbols pulse urgently on the terminal display. The flashing lights and loud siren appear to relate to the facility's nuclear power core. A message prints out on the display.
Systems are super-charged despite the security alert. Equipment beneath my feet buzzes and whirrs with a high intensity. The terminal blinks a warning.
The First Spawn watches you underling. Cower and despair! The First Spawn watches you underling. Cower and despair! The First Spawn watches you underling. Cower and despair!
The Gek First Spawn destroy the pirate! Destroy the pirate! Obey!
The Monolith disappears. The landscape around me seems the same, but somehow the planetary vegetation has moved. Sitting central to where the mysterious stone once stood is a red glowing orb.

The Monolith stands forlorn and seemingly forgotten. If I strain, I can see faint marks in the ground where ancient tribes would once come to worship and commune with the edifice. A gust of alien breeze carries a faint whisper of a voice. I struggle to hear it.
The air is compromised. My entry has allowed the overwhelming atmospheric heat to overwhelm sensitive systems. Even the primary terminal is failing beneath my finger-tips.
The alarm has locked the terminal. A message displays itself letter-by-letter on the screen.
Apply override chip or Cut input wires
The alarms blares, and the terminal in front of me is scrambled. Through the flickering of the corrupted display I can just about make out a message:
The alert has obscured the information on the primary terminal. I can only make out a few words.
The aura that fills the air begins to thicken as I approach the monolith. My vision narrows, my hearing grows faint and muffled. A lone voice cries out through the fog.
Do nothing or Offer your own arm
The control terminal before me appears to be for some sort of deep-level mining system. However, all systems have stalled. The screen flashes a readout:
The facility acted as a central upload point for Korvax scans from a thousand worlds, collating their data in an attempt to understand the underlying mechanics of the universe.
The facility acted as a local base for raiding parties against the system's Sentinels.
The facility acted as a staging ground for what appears to have been an unprovoked Gek attack against something called an 'Atlas Interface'.
Delete records or Alert Gek Trade Federation
The facility allowed for the quarantine and processing of Korvax minds to and from their central Convergence.
Wipe system or Comfort the Korvax
The facility appears to have been in the process of researching chemical and biological weapons before a containment failure killed all those who worked here.
Sell to Gek or Sell to Korvax
The facility contains records of temporal anomalies and reported sightings of time travellers. The majority of these appear to be Gek or Korvax, often bearing advanced technology.
The facility is processing a signal that emanates from a distant location deep in space. Endless processing units are combining to crack the code of a strange mathematical language.
The facility remains operational despite my intrusion. This terminal appears to control the central production line. A readout on the display displays a status warning:
The facility seems to have been a meeting place for multiple Korvax factions, uploading and downloading from multiple bodies during tense diplomatic and war-time situations.
The facility's logs show the arrival of a new Vy'keen recruit two weeks ago. There are no records of anyone arriving or leaving since.
Locate origin point or Alert Vy'keen
The facility's machinery lies still, halted by the emergency shutdown. A short message blinks on the control terminal.
The facility's production harvest is underway. I can speed up systems by boosting some of the machinery operating below me.
The factory appears to produce replacement parts for the exosuits of the alien Korvax, spitting out face mask after face mask, arms, datapads, even feet.
The factory is unlike the other Korvax facilities I have seen. It does not appear to produce machines or files, but strange reams of a plastic substance, covered in precise sequences of dots.
Shut down production or Report to Korvax authorities
The factory produces components for starships, fabricating them using the resources available on this world.
Attempt download or Wait and watch
The factory produces components for starships, fabricating them with the resources available on this world.
Alert Gek Trade Federation or Demand bribe from Gek
The factory produces everyday implements for the Gek. Eating utensils for their meals, spray to keep their skin from drying out in alien atmospheres, pheromone bottles, and so forth.
Search for technology or Shut down production
The factory recycles bundles of clothing and other materials harvested throughout the galaxy, spitting out new items for Gek exosuits.
Report to Gek or Report to Korvax
The factory stands vacant, producing nothing. The production lines have long since ceased, and though the alarm sounds, it is unclear why.
Start production or Alert Korvax authorities

The giant mouth of an ancient hound suddenly emerges through the face of the monolith. It opens its jaws wide, and foul-smelling spittle streaks my visor. My nausea is tempered by the sight of valuable commodities balanced on its giant tongue.
The ground in front of the monolith is indented by the knees of a thousand ancient pilgrims who once knelt here.
The inside of the planet is hollow, and I'm standing at the base of its vast bowl. Around me the roots of trees push upwards from uncovered alien soil.
The installation has been hacked. A coded transmission has breached security and is stealing data.
Block orbital signal or Report intrusion

The light of the flowing through the monolith is strangely comforting. I hear a deep and steady drone, reassuring and familiar. The sounds - these words - lull me, and my vision swims as I fall into their embrace...
The monolith crackles as I approach, arcing through the air. I hear the voice of the Korvax Echoes, and I close my eyes...
The monolith has the smell of burnt metal and heavy industry. Strange runes swirl and transform, forcing an image deep into my mind.
The monolith lets forth a silent scream. Words rage from the distant past, inserting themselves into my brain. My vision begins to swim.
The monolith rips like paper, opening a window to another world. It is laced with a giant web. Just within my reach, an ancient warrior lies cocooned.
The monolith shows images of creatures lying dead before it. Each sacrificed, butchered and offered up to whatever Gods were once worshipped here.

The monolith's glyphs take on a faint yellow tinge, then flicker and disappear. It has no power: the mysterious forces that fuel these stones are weak. I hear a faint crackling whisper on the planetary breeze.
The monolith, alive with , shows me a galaxy of stars, glittering points of light in all directions. I hear a voice that hums with the words of millions.
Remember the flare or Forget the flare or Do nothing
The noise of gas being flushed through systems beneath my feet can be heard over the noise of the alert. An automated report flashes onto the terminal.
The outpost appears to have been in the middle of complex planetary scan. Alarms sound against my intrusion, but the operation continues. I attempt to make sense of the output.
The outpost has gone into emergency lockdown. Something must have been damaged during my entry.
The outpost is abandoned, its alarms still blaring a warning to souls long-dead.
Download data or Report to Vy'keen
The outpost is ancient, even by the standards of the Vy'keen. Its environment is calibrated to preserve the data within.
Take technology or Search for Traveller records
The primary terminal is non-responsive, but comms seem open.
The pull of the monolith is irresistable. The sings to me, desperate to be heard. I reach out, ready to accept its vision.
The screen is a jumble of words, few of which aren't drowned in static.
The security alarm hasn't impacted production. Below my feet unseen equipment prepares the mineral harvest.
The security alert is scrambling the screen. All that is visible is a chaotic jumble of alien words.
The security alert that's firing is jamming the terminal. Static covers most of the screen, obscuring nearly all relevant information.
The security breach has dimmed the terminal, but when I concentrate I can make out a few words etched onto the screen...
The security breach has scrambled the screen, but some text is still legible.
The terminal displays the logs of numerous financial transactions and trade deals conducted from this facility over the last few months.
The terminal flashes an urgent warning. Some vital part of the facility has been compromised by the security alert.

The terminal reveals that this installation produces enzymes and fluids required for Vy'keen tattoos. It is unclear how the pigment is generated. There is no record of any inbound supplies of ink or fluid. Various aliens have arrived, but there is neither evidence of their presense nor their departure.
The terminal shows a variety of motionless lifeforms standing in colossal rows in the darkness beneath the factory.
The wail of an alarm fills my ears, but the system is not reacting to my intrusion. Someone else has been here and modified this terminal before. I struggle to decipher the data on the terminal.

A highly-advanced upgrade for the Pulse Engine, vastly increasing interplanetary speed.

This grey-market electronics module disables critical safety and pilot-assistance modules usually baked into the starship's fly-by-wire control system. Despite its dubious legal status and its implication in a series of high-speed asteroid impacts, this module remains popular with smugglers, mercenaries, and others who think of themselves as advanced pilots.
Provides increased manoeuvrability and longer boosts during spaceflight.
A highly-tuned version of the conventional starship Pulse Engine. Wavefront occupancy has been pushed to the limit, creating a pulse experience that is both efficient and highly responsive.

A high-performance solar sail, deployed automatically during flight. This advanced propulsion device generates an electric field within the sails themselves, allowing the starship to build momentum from the solar wind.
Vital launch and landing gear system.
Upgrades the starship launch systems, decreasing the fuel cost of takeoff.
Photovoltaic panels fitted to the starship Launch Thrusters allow for a slow trickle charge while the ship is not in operation.

A custom-made launch control system for high-performance starships. Sensitive gyroscopes and specialised control circuits plot custom take-off routines for increased launch speed and efficiency.
A device that modulates standard starship communication signals to enable the transport of matter as well as data.
FTL propulsion drive that allows starship to attain warp speed and jump between neighbouring systems.
Upgrades the hyperdrive's core bounding magnets, preventing rapid disassembly when attempting to reach rare-class red stellar bodies.
Upgrades the hyperdrive's shield integrity, preventing reality glitches when attempting to reach rare-class green stellar bodies.
Upgrades the hyperdrive's computational matrix,  preventing temporal anomalies when attempting to reach rare-class blue stellar bodies.
Sideloads a resonant memory packet into your warp computer,  allowing the ship to pass through the dissonant space surrounding purple stellar bodies.
A significant upgrade to the Hyperdrive that allows an instantaneous warp even while conventional systems are blocked by starship combat. Access to the emergency warp system is via the Quick Menu.
This experimental drive augments conventional hyperdrive technology by distorting local geometry at the point of warp initialisation, boosting range and efficiency far beyond standard drives.
A specially tuned resonance jammer, designed to interfere with the remote cargo scans deployed by system authorities in the search for smuggled goods.
Energy shield that protects spacecraft from laser fire, in-flight projectiles and accidental space debris interaction.
Adds a layer of superheated shielding to the starship's defense array, vaporising incoming fire.
A long range starship weapon, capable of delivering a highly explosive torpedo across massive distances.
Expands the loading chamber of the starship Rocket Launcher, improving exhaust performance and allowing for significantly faster heat recovery.
A destructive starship projectile launcher, the weapons system of choice for the interstellar trader and pirate alike.
Replaces the conventional Photon Cannon optics with an experimental glass array, boosting combat performance.
A high-energy beam weapon for ship-to-ship combat.
Rewires the Phase Beam with nanite-based circuitry, bypassing conventional reality limits on laser power.
A powerful starship weapon, capable of delivering extreme destruction at close range.
Overhauls the firing mechanism of the Positron Ejector, resulting in faster, more accurate particles.
A rapid fire starship weapon that launches superheated globes of liquid metal at hostile targets. These projectiles are extremely effective against unshielded starship hulls.

Replaces the heat sink of the Cyclotron Ballista by encompassing the entire unit with a heat-absorbing megastructure. Heat output is recycled to boost combat efficiency.

A salty membrane encases the ship, dramatically increasing its natural buoyancy.
Filaments of sinew and neuron warp and weave across the ship, their complex geometry darting between the visible world and some unfathomable dimension beyond.
